title: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
problem: An attempt to execute .map() was made on a variable that is undefined or null during render.
likely_cause: The list state is populated asynchronously (e.g. from an API call) and defaults to undefined on initial mount, causing the component to crash before the fetch completes.
fix_steps: 1. Provide a safe initial state of an empty array: `useState([])` instead of `useState()`.
2. Add optional chaining (`items?.map(...)`) or an explicit guard clause (`if (!items) return <Spinner />;`).
3. Verify that the API response actually returns an array rather than an object containing the array (e.g., `res.data.items`).
extra_tips: TypeScript can catch this at compile time: define your state type explicitly with `useState<Item[]>([])`. When working with nested payloads, use `Array.isArray(data)` before mapping.
prevention_checklist: Always initialize collection state with [] instead of undefined/null.
Add TypeScript types to API response payloads.
Implement Skeleton or Loading state while network requests are pending.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — Array.prototype.map() & Optional Chaining

title: CORS Policy Blocked: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' Header
problem: The browser blocks client-side fetch/axios requests to a third-party or local backend API due to Same-Origin Policy enforcement.
likely_cause: The target API server did not return an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header matching your web app's origin (e.g. http://localhost:3000 vs http://localhost:8000), or rejected the preflight OPTIONS request.
fix_steps: 1. For local development: configure a development proxy in `vite.config.ts` or `next.config.js` to route `/api/*` requests through the same origin.
2. For production: configure the backend server to include the CORS header `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://yourfrontend.com` and handle `OPTIONS` requests.
3. If sending Authorization headers or cookies, ensure backend sets `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type`.
code_before:
// ❌ Broken: Direct cross-origin request rejected by browser
fetch('http://localhost:8000/api/users');
extra_tips: CORS is an entirely browser-enforced security mechanism. Tools like Postman or curl will succeed because they are not running in a web browser context. Never use 'no-cors' mode expecting to read JSON data.
prevention_checklist: Use Vite/Next.js reverse proxies during local development.
Ensure backend handles CORS middleware before any authentication middleware.
Never commit 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' when using credentials.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)

title: CSS Centering: Div or Modal Not Centered on Screen
problem: An HTML element fails to center horizontally or vertically within its parent container or the viewport.
likely_cause: The parent element lacks explicit height (defaulting to content height 0), or flex/grid alignment properties were applied to the child instead of the parent container.
fix_steps: 1. Use CSS Grid on parent: `display: grid; place-items: center; min-height: 100vh;` (cleanest one-line solution).
2. Or use Flexbox on parent: `display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; min-height: 100vh;`.
3. Ensure the parent container has an explicit height such as `min-height: 100vh` or `min-height: 100dvh`.
extra_tips: For modern mobile browsers, prefer `min-height: 100dvh` over `100vh` to avoid content shifting when the URL bar collapses.
prevention_checklist: Check if parent has height before trying to vertically center.
Apply flex/grid container properties to parent, not children.
Use modern CSS Grid place-items: center for fast layout.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — Centering in CSS

title: Too Many Re-renders: useEffect Runs in an Infinite Loop
trigger_patterns: useeffect runs in an infinite loop
problem: Component re-renders continuously until React halts execution with 'Maximum update depth exceeded' or 'Too many re-renders'.
likely_cause: A state update function (`setCount` or `setData`) is executed directly inside the component body, or inside a `useEffect` whose dependency array contains an object/function reference that changes on every render.
fix_steps: 1. Never call `setState` unconditionally in the render body.
2. Check `useEffect` dependencies: pass an empty array `[]` for mount-only effects.
3. If updating based on previous state, use the updater function: `setCount(prev => prev + 1)` instead of adding `count` to dependencies.
4. Memoize object/array dependencies with `useMemo` or functions with `useCallback`.
extra_tips: If your effect is just calculating a value from other props/state, don't use state + effect at all! Calculate it during rendering as derived state.
prevention_checklist: Prefer derived state over sync useEffect + setState.
Use functional state updates (prev => next).
Avoid objects or array literals inside dependency arrays.
source_title: React.dev — You Might Not Need an Effect

title: React Hydration Mismatch (Server vs Client HTML Mismatch)
trigger_patterns: did not match what was rendered on the server
problem: Next.js or React 18/19 throws an error warning that the server-rendered HTML differed from the initial client render tree.
likely_cause: The component rendered client-only dynamic values (like `window.innerWidth`, `localStorage`, `Math.random()`, or `new Date()`) directly in JSX during initial render before mounting.
fix_steps: 1. Defer reading client-only values into a `useState` initialized to null, and populate inside `useEffect`.
2. For timestamps, render a static placeholder or suppress warning on that specific tag with `suppressHydrationWarning={true}`.

3. Verify that your HTML structure is valid (e.g. no `

` containing `

` or `` without ``).
extra_tips:
Invalid HTML tags are the second most common hydration trigger. In HTML specs, `

` cannot contain block elements like `

` or `
`; browsers auto-close the `

`, throwing off React's DOM tree matching.
prevention_checklist: Never read window, document, or localStorage in component render body.
Check browser console for the exact diff tags highlighted by React.
Validate HTML semantics to prevent auto-closing tags.

title: CSS Z-Index Stacking Context Trap (Element Renders Behind)
problem: An element with a high `z-index` (e.g. 9999) still renders behind another element with a lower or no z-index.
likely_cause: An ancestor element creates an isolated Stacking Context (via `opacity < 1`, `transform`, `filter`, `perspective`, or `isolation: isolate`), trapping all descendants inside.
fix_steps: 1. Mount overlays/modals directly into `document.body` using `ReactDOM.createPortal`.
2. Inspect parent CSS for `transform`, `filter`, `opacity < 1`, or `will-change` properties.
3. Ensure the element or its positioning ancestor has `position: relative`, `absolute`, or `fixed` (z-index does not work on static elements).
extra_tips: Use the Chrome DevTools 'Layers' or 'Elements > Styles' panel to view which parent creates the stacking context.
prevention_checklist: Always use React Portals for modals, tooltips, and floating menus.
Remember: z-index is relative to parent stacking context, not global page.
Avoid unnecessary transforms on container wrappers.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — Understanding CSS Stacking Context

title: Flexbox Child Overflowing Container (text-overflow: ellipsis broken)
problem: A text element inside a flex container refuses to truncate with ellipsis and instead forces the parent container to stretch horizontally.
likely_cause: By default, flex items have `min-width: auto`, which prevents them from shrinking below their intrinsic content size.
fix_steps: 1. Add `min-width: 0;` to the flex child element.
2. Ensure the text element has `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;`.
3. If nested in multiple flex containers, apply `min-width: 0;` down the hierarchy.
extra_tips: In CSS Grid, the exact equivalent issue occurs with `grid-template-columns`. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` instead of `1fr` to enable child truncation.
prevention_checklist: Apply min-width: 0 to any flex item intended to truncate.
Use minmax(0, 1fr) in CSS Grid columns containing text.
Test responsive layouts with long unbroken strings like URLs.

title: Warning: Each child in a list should have a unique 'key' prop
trigger_patterns: each child in a list should have a unique key prop
problem: React browser console displays a warning about missing keys when rendering an array of elements.
likely_cause: Elements rendered inside a `.map()` loop lack a unique and stable `key` attribute on their outermost JSX element, causing React reconciliation issues.
fix_steps: 1. Add a unique, stable ID from your data (e.g. `key={item.id}`).
2. Avoid using the array index (`key={index}`) if the list items can be reordered, filtered, or deleted.
3. Place the `key` prop on the top-most JSX node inside the map callback, even if it is a `<React.Fragment key={item.id}>`.
extra_tips: Using the index as a key causes subtle bugs with input state preservation and animations when items are sorted or removed.
prevention_checklist: Always supply stable string/number ids for list keys.
Avoid Math.random() as key - it forces full remount on every render.
Use React.Fragment with key syntax: <React.Fragment key={id}>.

title: Warning: Component changing uncontrolled input to be controlled
trigger_patterns: changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled
problem: React warns in console that an `<input>` switched from uncontrolled to controlled (or vice versa).
likely_cause: The input's `value` prop was initialized to `undefined` or `null`, so React treated it as uncontrolled until asynchronous data populated the state.
fix_steps: 1. Initialize your form state with an empty string `""` instead of `undefined` or `null`.
2. Pass a fallback value to the input: `value={form.name ?? ''}`.
3. Ensure the `onChange` handler updates state synchronously.
extra_tips: For large forms, consider using React Hook Form or Formik which manage input registration and default values automatically.
prevention_checklist: Always provide default string values for form inputs.
Use nullish coalescing `value={val ?? ''}`.
Never leave input value as undefined.

title: Form Button Reloads Page / Submits on Click
problem: Clicking a button inside a `<form>` unexpectedly refreshes the browser page and clears the state.
likely_cause: The HTML standard defines the default `type` of a `<button>` inside a `<form>` as `type="submit"`. If clicked without `e.preventDefault()`, it submits the form via HTTP GET/POST.
fix_steps: 1. If the button is not meant to submit, add `type="button"` explicitly.
2. If it is the submit button, attach an `onSubmit` handler to the `<form>` and call `e.preventDefault()`.
3. Never rely on button `onClick` for form submission; handle `onSubmit` on the form element itself.
code_before:
// ❌ Broken: Default type is 'submit', reloads page
<form>
  <input value={name} />
  <button onClick={handleCustomAction}>Cancel</button>
</form>
code_after:
// ✅ Fixed: Explicitly declare type='button'
<form onSubmit={e => { e.preventDefault(); handleSubmit(); }}>
  <input value={name} />
  <button type="button" onClick={handleCustomAction}>Cancel</button>
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
extra_tips: Adding `type="button"` to secondary buttons also enables keyboard users to trigger them with the Space key while avoiding accidental form submissions.
prevention_checklist: Always specify type='button' or type='submit' on every <button>.
Attach submission handlers to <form onSubmit={...}> not <button onClick={...}>.
Call e.preventDefault() in form submit handlers.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — The HTML <button> Element

title: HTTP 404 Not Found on API Fetch or SPA Client-Side Route Refresh
trigger_patterns: failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404
problem: Network requests return 404 Not Found, or refreshing the page on routes like `/dashboard` returns 404 from the web server.
likely_cause: Either the API endpoint URL or base URL path has a typo, or the production web server (Nginx/Vercel) lacks fallback routing to `index.html` for single-page applications.
fix_steps: 1. Inspect the Network tab in DevTools to check the exact requested URL, method, and base path.
2. For API calls: verify trailing slash consistency (`/api/users/` vs `/api/users`).
3. For SPA page refreshes: configure your web server (Nginx, Netlify `_redirects`, or Apache `.htaccess`) to rewrite all non-file routes to `index.html`.
extra_tips: Always check whether environment variables like `VITE_API_URL` are actually defined in your production build.
prevention_checklist: Ensure SPA web servers rewrite non-file requests to index.html.
Check exact URL paths and query parameters in DevTools Network tab.
Define centralized API client with base URL configuration.

title: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error & Handling Unhandled Rejections
problem: An API call fails with status code 500, and client code breaks trying to parse missing JSON data.
likely_cause: The backend server crashed or failed an unhandled exception (e.g. malformed JSON body, database connection error, missing required payload field).
fix_steps: 1. Open DevTools Network tab, click the failed request, and view the 'Response' tab for server error details.
2. Wrap your `fetch` or `axios` call with proper error handling checking `response.ok` before calling `response.json()`.
3. Display a user-friendly error message rather than crashing the whole screen.
extra_tips: Many production backends return HTML error pages on 500s. Always check `res.ok` before invoking `.json()` to avoid `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'`.
prevention_checklist: Always check response.ok in fetch before calling response.json().
Use try/catch around async network calls.
Display toast notifications or fallback UI for server errors.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — 500 Internal Server Error

title: SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<', '<!DOCTYPE '... is not valid JSON
problem: Calling `response.json()` fails with a SyntaxError pointing to an opening HTML `<` character.
likely_cause: The server returned an HTML webpage (such as an Nginx 404/502 page, a single-page app index.html, or an authentication redirect) instead of the expected JSON payload.
fix_steps: 1. Check the response Content-Type header before parsing as JSON: `res.headers.get('content-type')`.
2. Inspect the failed request in DevTools Network tab to see the actual returned HTML.
3. Verify that the API route exists and you didn't miss `/api/` in the URL prefix.
extra_tips: This frequently happens when a client-side SPA route rewrite catches your API call because of a mismatched endpoint path.
prevention_checklist: Validate Content-Type header contains application/json.
Verify API proxy rules match all intended endpoints.
Log the first 100 characters of raw body on failure for fast diagnosis.

title: UnhandledPromiseRejection: Uncaught (in promise) Error
problem: Browser console reports `Uncaught (in promise)` and breaks subsequent execution flows.
likely_cause: An async function or Promise returned a rejected state (e.g. `fetch` network failure), but no `.catch()` handler or `try/catch` block caught the rejection.
fix_steps: 1. Wrap all `await` calls in `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` blocks.
2. For chainable promises, always append `.catch(err => ...)` at the end of the chain.
3. Register a global `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...)` handler for telemetry and error tracking.
extra_tips: Remember that `fetch()` only rejects on actual network failure (DNS, offline, CORS); it does NOT reject on HTTP 404 or 500 statuses.
prevention_checklist: Wrap async/await in try/catch.
Add unhandledrejection event listener in app root.
Check res.ok since fetch does not reject on 4xx/5xx.

title: React Hooks Violation: Rendered fewer (or more) hooks than expected
trigger_patterns: hooks can only be called inside the body
problem: React crashes with 'Rendered fewer hooks than expected' or 'Invalid hook call'.
likely_cause: A React Hook (`useState`, `useEffect`, `useMemo`) was placed inside a conditional `if` statement, a loop, or after an early `return` statement.
fix_steps: 1. Move all hook calls to the very top level of your component function, before any conditional logic or early returns.
2. Never call hooks inside loops, conditionals, or nested functions.
3. Ensure the component name starts with a capital letter (PascalCase) or is a custom hook starting with `use`.
extra_tips: React relies on the exact execution order of hook calls to maintain state index between renders. Any alteration in call order breaks internal fiber state pointers.
prevention_checklist: Use eslint-plugin-react-hooks in your linter.
Call all hooks at the very top of the component.
Never put hooks inside if statements, loops, or event callbacks.

title: Stale Closure in useEffect or Event Listener: State Not Updating
problem: An asynchronous timer (`setInterval`) or event listener accesses an old, outdated value of state that never changes.
likely_cause: The callback closed over the state variable from its initial render, and the dependency array was left empty `[]` without refreshing the closure.
fix_steps: 1. Use functional state updates (`setCount(c => c + 1)`) so you don't need the state variable in the closure.
2. If reading current state inside a listener, store the latest value in a `useRef`.
3. Add the missing state variable to the `useEffect` dependency array and clean up the interval on unmount.
extra_tips: The functional update pattern `setState(prev => ...)` is both faster and cleaner because it eliminates the need to restart the timer every second.
prevention_checklist: Use prev => next in setState whenever updating based on previous value.
Use useRef for mutable values needed inside event listeners.
Always return cleanup functions from useEffect intervals/listeners.

title: Race Condition in Fetch Requests: Out-of-Order API Responses
problem: When typing quickly in a search bar or switching tabs rapidly, an earlier slow API request resolves AFTER a later fast request, displaying outdated results.
likely_cause: Network latency is non-deterministic; without cancellation, the slowest request overwrites the most recent request's state.
fix_steps: 1. Create an `AbortController` inside `useEffect` and pass `signal: controller.signal` to `fetch`.
2. In the `useEffect` cleanup return function, call `controller.abort()`.
3. Catch and ignore `AbortError` so it doesn't log unnecessary errors to console.
4. Alternatively, use modern server-state libraries like TanStack Query / SWR.
extra_tips: Debouncing the input by 300ms using a small timer further reduces server load and avoids unnecessary network requests.
prevention_checklist: Use AbortController in useEffect fetch calls.
Debounce auto-complete and search inputs.
Consider TanStack Query for automatic query cancellation.

title: CSS position: sticky Not Working (Element Scrolls Away)
problem: An element with `position: sticky` scrolls off the page instead of anchoring at its defined threshold.
likely_cause: Either no threshold property (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) was defined, or an ancestor element has `overflow: hidden`, `overflow: auto`, or `overflow: scroll` which clips the scrolling context.
fix_steps: 1. Ensure at least one positioning threshold is declared (e.g. `top: 0;`).
2. Inspect all ancestor parent elements in DevTools for `overflow: hidden`, `clip`, or `auto` and remove them from the scrolling container.
3. Verify that the parent container has enough height to allow scrolling (sticky elements only stick within their direct parent).
extra_tips: A quick JavaScript DevTools snippet to find rogue overflow parents: `let el = $0; while (el) { const s = getComputedStyle(el); if (s.overflow !== 'visible') console.log(el); el = el.parentElement; }`.
prevention_checklist: Always set top, bottom, left or right on sticky elements.
Ensure parent containers do not have overflow: hidden.
Remember sticky elements cannot stick outside their immediate parent's bounding box.

title: Mobile 100vh Layout Jump / Content Cut Off by Browser Address Bar
problem: On mobile devices (iOS Safari & Chrome Android), a full-height container (`height: 100vh`) is partly covered by the dynamic browser address bar, causing awkward scrolling.
likely_cause: The traditional CSS `vh` unit calculates against the maximum viewport height assuming the browser address bar is hidden.
fix_steps: 1. Use the modern Dynamic Viewport Height unit: `min-height: 100dvh;`.
2. Provide a fallback for older browsers: `min-height: 100vh; min-height: 100dvh;`.
3. For fixed overlays, ensure `bottom: 0; top: 0;` or use `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.
extra_tips: Use `padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` when positioning elements near the bottom on iPhone devices with home indicator bars.
prevention_checklist: Use 100dvh instead of 100vh for full-height screens.
Include safe-area-inset padding for iPhone home indicator bars.
Test responsive designs on real mobile touch devices.
source_title: web.dev — The Large, Small, and Dynamic Viewport Units

title: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'property')
problem: Runtime crash when trying to access a property or method on a variable whose value evaluates to `null`.
likely_cause: An object state (like `user`, `config`, or a DOM ref) is initialized to `null` or fetched asynchronously, and properties are accessed before resolution.
fix_steps: 1. Use optional chaining: `user?.profile?.name`.
2. Use nullish coalescing to provide safe fallbacks: `user?.name ?? 'Guest'`.
3. Place an early return loading guard at the top of the component.
extra_tips: TypeScript strict null checks (`strictNullChecks: true`) will warn you at compile-time whenever an expression could potentially be null.
prevention_checklist: Enable strictNullChecks in tsconfig.json.
Use optional chaining (?.) on nested objects.
Provide skeleton loaders while user data loads.

title: TypeError: Assignment to constant variable
problem: JavaScript runtime throws TypeError when attempting to reassign a variable declared with `const`.
likely_cause: A variable was declared with `const` and later reassigned with the `=` operator, or mutated inside a loop counter.
fix_steps: 1. Change `const` to `let` if the primitive variable needs to be reassigned.
2. If working with objects or arrays, you CAN mutate their properties (`arr.push()` or `obj.key = val`) without reassigning the variable itself.
3. In React state, never reassign local variables; use the setState setter function.
extra_tips: In modern functional JavaScript, consider using a ternary expression: `const total = hasDiscount ? base * 0.9 : base;` to preserve immutability.
prevention_checklist: Use let when variable will be reassigned.
Use const with ternary expressions instead of if-reassignment.
Never mutate React state variables directly.

title: NaN (Not-a-Number) in Calculations or UI Displays
problem: Mathematical calculations result in `NaN` or display `NaN` on the screen.
likely_cause: Performing arithmetic operations (`-`, `*`, `/`) with `undefined`, `null`, or an unparsed string value (e.g. from an HTML `<input>` value).
fix_steps: 1. Parse numeric inputs explicitly: `Number(inputVal)` or `parseFloat(inputVal)`.
2. Guard against missing or undefined values: `Number(price || 0)`.
3. Use `Number.isNaN(val)` to check and sanitize before rendering.
extra_tips: Remember that `<input type="number" />` still produces a string in `e.target.value`. In React, use `e.target.valueAsNumber` for instant numeric conversion.
prevention_checklist: Use e.target.valueAsNumber for HTML number inputs.
Provide default 0 for mathematical operands.
Format final numeric results with .toFixed(2) or Intl.NumberFormat.

title: Warning: Can't perform a React state update on an unmounted component
trigger_patterns: can't perform a react state update on an unmounted component
problem: React warns that `setState` was called after a component was already unmounted from the DOM.
likely_cause: An async API fetch, `setTimeout`, or WebSocket message resolves after the user navigated away from the screen.
fix_steps: 1. Cancel the async operation on unmount using `AbortController`.
2. Clear any active `setTimeout` or `setInterval` in the `useEffect` cleanup function.
3. Alternatively, track mount status with an `isMounted` flag inside the effect.
extra_tips: While React 18 removed the hard console warning, lingering promises still waste memory and can trigger subtle background errors.
prevention_checklist: Always return cleanup functions from useEffect.
Cancel fetch requests using AbortController.
Clear timers with clearTimeout/clearInterval.

title: CSS Margin Collapse: Unexpected Vertical Gaps or Ignored Margins
problem: Top or bottom margins between adjacent elements combine into a single margin, or a child's top margin spills outside its parent container.
likely_cause: CSS margin collapsing occurs when block elements in normal flow have adjoining vertical margins without padding, borders, or inline content separating them.
fix_steps: 1. Modern fix: use Flexbox or CSS Grid with the `gap` property instead of vertical margins.
2. If keeping block layout, add `padding-top: 1px;` or `border-top: 1px solid transparent;` to the parent.
3. Or set `overflow: hidden;` or `display: flow-root;` on the parent to create a new Block Formatting Context (BFC).
extra_tips: Flex and Grid containers NEVER experience margin collapsing. Whenever possible, replace `margin-bottom` with parent `gap`.
prevention_checklist: Use flex/grid gap instead of vertical margins on children.
Use display: flow-root on parent if traditional block flow is needed.
Remember margins never collapse horizontally.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — Mastering Margin Collapsing

title: CSS Grid Items Overflowing Container / Not Responsive
problem: CSS Grid columns do not adjust to small screens, causing horizontal scrolling and container breaking.
likely_cause: Grid columns were declared with fixed pixel widths (`grid-template-columns: 300px 300px`) or `1fr` columns with rigid child content.
fix_steps: 1. Use responsive auto-fitting columns: `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr));`.
2. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` instead of raw `1fr` if children contain long strings.
3. Combine with `gap: 1.5rem;` for automatic wrapping without media queries.
extra_tips: The expression `minmax(min(100%, 280px), 1fr))` prevents overflow even on tiny screens under 280px wide.
prevention_checklist: Use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) for responsive card grids.
Avoid hardcoded fixed column numbers when cards must wrap.
Add minmax(0, 1fr) to prevent text overflow.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — Realizing Common Layouts Using CSS Grid

title: Accessibility Violation: Form Input Missing Associated Label or ARIA
trigger_patterns: form control does not have an associated label
problem: Lighthouse or screen readers report that an input field lacks an associated `<label>` or accessible name.
likely_cause: Using a standalone `<input>` without linking it to a `<label htmlFor="id">` or omitting `aria-label`.
fix_steps: 1. Wrap the `<input>` inside a `<label>` element, or link with `<label htmlFor="userId">` and `<input id="userId">`.
2. If a visible label is not desired visually, use `aria-label="Search"` or a visually-hidden CSS utility (`sr-only`).
3. Never rely solely on the `placeholder` attribute as a replacement for a label.
code_before:
/* ❌ Broken: Placeholder is not an accessible label */
<input type="text" placeholder="Search..." />
extra_tips: Placeholders vanish when the user types, making them unusable for cognitive accessibility. An accessible label guarantees screen reader support.
prevention_checklist: Always provide label htmlFor='id' matching input id.
Use aria-label on icon buttons and search bars.
Do not use placeholder as the sole label.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — How to Structure a Web Form

title: Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): Image Jumps and Shifts Content on Load
problem: As images load, existing text and layout jump downward, producing poor Lighthouse Core Web Vitals (CLS) scores.
likely_cause: The `` tag lacks explicit `width` and `height` HTML attributes or a CSS `aspect-ratio`, forcing the browser to allocate 0 height until image dimensions are downloaded.
fix_steps: 1. Add explicit `width` and `height` attributes to the `` tag: ``.
2. Add CSS responsive rule: `img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }` so the aspect ratio is preserved.
3. Alternatively, define CSS `aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;` on the image wrapper.
code_before: /* ❌ Broken: Browser allocates 0px height initially, causing jump */
code_after: /* ✅ Fixed: Explicit dimensions let browser reserve space */
extra_tips: Modern browsers calculate the aspect ratio from the HTML `width` and `height` attributes before downloading the image file, reserving the exact space in layout.
prevention_checklist: Always set width and height attributes on tags.
Use CSS max-width: 100% and height: auto.
Use aspect-ratio for dynamic responsive containers.

title: Content Security Policy (CSP) Violation: Blocked Inline Script or Font
problem: Browser console shows error: `Refused to execute inline script because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive...`.
likely_cause: The website's CSP header restricts script or stylesheet execution from unauthorized inline blocks, third-party CDNs, or eval statements.
fix_steps: 1. Move inline `<script>` code into external bundled JavaScript files.
2. If using Vite or Next.js, configure a cryptographic `nonce` or hash in your CSP header.
3. Whitelist trusted CDN origins in your `Content-Security-Policy` header (e.g. `font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com`).
code_before:
<!-- ❌ Blocked by strict CSP -->
<script>
  window.analytics = { id: 123 }; // Inline script blocked!
</script>
code_after:
<!-- ✅ Fixed: Load via external bundled asset or supply nonce -->
<script type="module" src="/src/analytics.js"></script>
<!-- Or in server header: Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0m'; -->
extra_tips: Avoid adding `'unsafe-inline'` to production CSP headers, as it negates protection against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks.
prevention_checklist: Never use inline <script> or inline event handlers like onclick='...'.
Whitelist necessary CDN domains explicitly in CSP.
Generate dynamic nonces for server-rendered inline scripts.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — Content Security Policy (CSP)

title: Mixed Content: Insecure HTTP Request on Secure HTTPS Page
trigger_patterns: was loaded over https, but requested an insecure
problem: Browser refuses to load scripts, images, or API endpoints on an HTTPS website, logging a Mixed Content error.
likely_cause: The main website is served over HTTPS, but attempts to fetch assets or API data via unencrypted `http://` protocols.
fix_steps: 1. Upgrade the resource URL to `https://`.
2. Use protocol-relative URLs (`//api.example.com`) or relative paths (`/api/data`).
3. Add the header `Content-Security-Policy: upgrade-insecure-requests;` to auto-upgrade HTTP requests.
code_before:
// ❌ Broken: http request on https domain blocked
const API_URL = 'http://api.mysite.com/v1';
code_after:
// ✅ Fixed: Use https protocol or domain proxy
const API_URL = 'https://api.mysite.com/v1';
extra_tips: Modern browsers actively block 'mixed active content' (scripts, fetch calls, iframes) to protect users from Man-In-The-Middle packet tampering.
prevention_checklist: Always use https:// for all external API endpoints and CDN URLs.
Configure upgrade-insecure-requests in CSP header.
Check environment variables for hardcoded http:// prefixes.
source_title: MDN Web Docs — What is Mixed Content?

title: DOMException: QuotaExceededError in localStorage.setItem()
problem: Calling `localStorage.setItem()` crashes with `DOMException: QuotaExceededError: Setting the value of 'x' exceeded the quota`.
likely_cause: The browser's localStorage quota (typically 5MB per origin) has been exceeded, often caused by caching large base64 images or massive JSON responses.
fix_steps: 1. Switch to `IndexedDB` (using libraries like `idb` or `localforage`) for datasets larger than a few megabytes.
2. Wrap `localStorage.setItem` in a `try/catch` block to handle full storage gracefully.
3. Implement an LRU eviction or expiration policy to purge stale cache entries.
code_before:
// ❌ Broken: Crashes app when 5MB limit is reached
localStorage.setItem('large_cache', JSON.stringify(heavyData));
extra_tips: Never store binary files, images, or offline database backups in localStorage. Use IndexedDB which supports hundreds of megabytes.
prevention_checklist: Never store large blobs or base64 images in localStorage.
Wrap localStorage.setItem in try/catch.
Use IndexedDB (localforage) for rich client-side caching.

title: CORS Error: 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' Cannot Be Wildcard '*' with Credentials
problem: Fetch with `{ credentials: 'include' }` or cookies fails with a CORS error stating that wildcard `*` origin is not permitted.
likely_cause: When a frontend sends HTTP cookies or credentials, the CORS specification strictly forbids the backend from returning `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.
fix_steps: 1. Configure backend server to echo the exact requesting origin (e.g. `http://localhost:3000` or `https://app.com`).
2. Set the backend header `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`.
3. If credentials (cookies) are not actually required, remove `credentials: 'include'` from the client fetch request.
extra_tips: Most backend CORS middlewares (like FastAPI CORSMiddleware or Express cors) take an `allow_origins=['https://app.com']` list to handle this automatically.
prevention_checklist: Specify exact domain in backend allow_origins when using credentials.
Enable Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true on backend.
Only send credentials: 'include' when cookies or sessions are needed.
